newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 13/14 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 13/14 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 13/14 percent in early trading on Friday from 11/12 percent at the opening, dealers said.
They said the raise in the overnight interbank rate was partly due to tighter liquidity because of weekly corporate tax payment and month-end factors.

One dealer said operators had expected the rate to remain as high as 20 percent following a sharp jump late on Thursday, but the central bank's injection of 328 billion rupiah helped increased liquidity and pushed the overnight rate down.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.50 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 15.38 percent against 8.34 percent on Wednesday.
